title: The top cities in the Asia Pacific in 2026
gist: Oxford Economics' 2026 Global Cities Index shows APAC cities rising: 396 APAC cities forecast to grow 2.7% a year, reaching 40% of the top-1,000 city GDP by 2050, with Tokyo and Australian cities leading and Kuala Lumpur, Shenzhen, Bengaluru, Ho Chi Minh City and Tashkent flagged as cities to watch.

themes.theme: Eastward shift of urban economic weight

insights.claim: Oxford forecasts real GDP growth across 396 Asia Pacific cities averaging 2.7% a year over 25 years, faster than any other region except Africa, lifting APAC to 40% of GDP of the world's 1,000 largest cities by 2050 from 35% today and 23% in 2001.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Structural tilt of global activity eastward supports long-run APAC allocation.
insights.locator: APAC's most advanced cities hold their ground

insights.claim: Tokyo ranks ninth in the index and is the world's second-largest city economy; five Australian capitals sit in the top 50 (Sydney 13th, Melbourne 16th, Brisbane 36th, Perth 44th, Canberra 45th), with Canberra first for Quality of Life.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Advanced-APAC hubs score on human capital and quality of life despite slow growth.

insights.claim: Singapore (29th), Seoul (38th) and Taipei (48th, new to the top 50) are at the heart of APAC's semiconductor industry, where AI-driven chip demand has supercharged their economies despite acutely ageing populations.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: AI chip cycle underpins top-tier Asian city economies; ageing is the offsetting headwind.
insights.locator: Rounding out Asia Pacific's highest-ranking cities

insights.claim: Kuala Lumpur (65th) is nearing the top 50 by leveraging human capital, lower operating costs, and expanding finance and tech sectors, and Ho Chi Minh City (205th) is expected to rank among the 50 fastest-growing cities over the next five years.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Southeast Asian second-tier hubs are cost-competitive alternatives.

insights.claim: Shenzhen is the highest-ranked mainland city at 93rd, the first Chinese city in the top 100, driven by commercialising robotics and green technologies, and is forecast to move from the 14th-largest to the 11th-largest metropolis by 2050.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Shenzhen is the tech-commercialisation engine of China's urban growth.
insights.locator: Shenzhen, our pick for mainland China

insights.claim: India will have the world's most populous city (Delhi) by 2050 and six of the top 10 fastest-growing cities by real GDP over 25 years, though weak Quality of Life and Environment scores keep its cities from top ranks; Bengaluru (311th) is a top-10 grower.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: India has the broadest urban growth runway, constrained by liveability.
insights.locator: No other country, however, comes close to India

insights.claim: Tashkent ranks 343rd but is in the top 10 for long-term GDP growth, reflecting Uzbekistan's economic liberalisation and WTO accession.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Central Asia is an overlooked frontier growth story.
insights.locator: The final Asia Pacific City to Watch
